name: Groq Cloud
tagline: The most generous no-card free tier left in 2026 — and the one place where "free" still means per-day tokens, not a trial coupon.
quota: A Free plan exists alongside the paid Developer plan, with per-model daily allowances rather than a credit wallet or trial balance. Note the exact free numbers are not separately published — see the caveat in `limits`.
limits: From Groq's official rate-limits page, per model: gpt-oss-120b / gpt-oss-20b / gpt-oss-safeguard-20b / qwen3.6-27b — 30 RPM, 1K RPD, 8K TPM, 200K TPD; qwen3.8-27b — same but 2M TPD; groq/compound and compound-mini — 30 RPM, 250 RPD, 70K TPM; llama-prompt-guard-2 22m/86m — 30 RPM, 14.4K RPD, 15K TPM, 500K TPD; whisper-large-v3 / -turbo — 20 RPM, 2K RPD, 7.2K ASH, 28.8K ASD; Orpheus TTS — 10 RPM, 100 RPD. CAVEAT: the page presents 'Free Plan Limits' and 'Developer Plan Limits' as two tabs and only one table is present in the page source, while the surrounding prose states 'the limits shown below are the base limits for the Developer plan'. The free tier may therefore be lower than the figures above — confirm your own numbers at console.groq.com/settings/limits after signup. Two things are unambiguous regardless: limits are enforced at the ORGANIZATION level (extra API keys do not raise them), and cached tokens do not count against limits.
expiry: Does not expire. Request counters reset daily; the free plan itself has no end date.
path: console.groq.com → sign up with Google or GitHub → Keys → Create API Key → copy it. No billing step appears anywhere in the flow.
code:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key="gsk_xxx",
    base_url="https://api.groq.com/openai/v1",
)

r = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-oss-120b",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}],
)
print(r.choices[0].message.content)
verdict: Still the best default free tier for a solo dev: no card, no expiry, fast inference, and an OpenAI-compatible endpoint you can swap in with one line. Two real caveats — Groq does not cleanly publish the Free plan's own numbers (the docs table may be showing Developer-plan values, so verify on your Limits page), and limits are organization-level, so you cannot multiply them with extra keys.

name: OpenRouter
tagline: One key in front of 18 genuinely free models — the fastest way to stop betting your prototype on a single vendor's free tier.
quota: 18 models with a `:free` suffix are callable at no cost (out of 396 models on the platform as of 2026-08-29). No credit card is needed to start; free variants are rate-limited instead of billed.
limits: Accounts that have purchased less than 10 credits: 20 requests/minute and 50 requests/day on `:free` models. Buy 10+ credits (about $10) and the daily cap jumps to 1,000 requests/day at the same 20 RPM. Rate limits are governed globally across your account — creating extra keys or accounts does not raise them. A negative account balance returns 402 even on free models. Cloudflare DDoS protection may also block abnormal bursts.
expiry: Does not expire. Daily request counters reset on the UTC day boundary.
path: openrouter.ai → sign in with Google/GitHub → Keys → Create Key → pick any model ending in `:free`. Add ~10 credits if 50 requests/day is too tight.
code:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key="sk-or-v1-xxx",
    base_url="https://openrouter.ai/api/v1",
)

r = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="google/gemma-4-31b-it:free",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}],
)
print(r.choices[0].message.content)
verdict: The best insurance policy in this list: one OpenAI-compatible key, 18 free models from different labs, and automatic fallback when an upstream provider is down. The hard ceiling is 50 requests/day until you spend $10 — fine for prototypes, useless for anything with real traffic. Also note the free lineup is volatile, with some models carrying live deprecation notices.
best_for: Testing a model before committing to a vendor

name: Cloudflare Workers AI
tagline: 10,000 free neurons a day on a serverless edge — generous for small models, and the frontier models are quietly gated behind a card.
quota: 10,000 Neurons per day at no charge, on the Workers Free plan. Neurons are Cloudflare's own compute unit, not tokens — a small model like llama-3.2-1b costs ~2,457 neurons per million input tokens, while llama-3.3-70b costs ~26,668 per million input and ~204,805 per million output. So 10K neurons/day is roughly 4M input tokens on a small model but under 50K output tokens on a 70B.
limits: All limits reset daily at 00:00 UTC; exceeding them fails the operation. Text generation, embeddings, image, audio and translation models are all covered. IMPORTANT: the flagship models require a paid billing method on a Workers Paid plan or prepaid AI Gateway credits — currently @cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6, @cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.7-code, @cf/zai-org/glm-5.2, @cf/zai-org/glm-5.3, @cf/zai-org/glm-5.3-flash, @cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash-0731, @cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-pro-0813.
expiry: Never expires as a plan; the 10,000-neuron allowance resets every day at 00:00 UTC.
path: dash.cloudflare.com → sign up (no card) → Workers & Pages → create a Worker → add an AI binding → call `env.AI.run()` from the Worker, or use the REST API with your Account ID and an API token.
code:
import os, requests

ACCOUNT = os.environ["CF_ACCOUNT_ID"]
TOKEN = os.environ["CF_API_TOKEN"]

r = requests.post(
    f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT}/ai/run/"
    "@cf/meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct-fp8-fast",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {TOKEN}"},
    json={"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]},
)
print(r.json()["result"]["response"])
verdict: Free, daily-refreshing and genuinely multi-modal (LLM, embeddings, Whisper, TTS, FLUX images) — but you are billed in neurons, a unit nobody can estimate in their head, and the daily budget is tiny once you touch a 70B model. Best used from inside a Worker, where it is genuinely zero-ops; weakest as a general-purpose chat API. The headline frontier models are card-gated, so do not come here expecting free DeepSeek V4 or Kimi.
best_for: Embeddings and reranking at the edge
Whisper transcription and cheap image generation

name: Cohere
tagline: A trial key that is free while Cohere issues one, but capped at 1,000 calls a month — useful for RAG plumbing, useless as a chat endpoint.
quota: Trial keys are free but limited to 1,000 API calls per month across the Chat API. Other endpoints are not capped by that monthly number — only by their own per-minute rates — which makes Embedding and Rerank the real reason to hold a trial key.
limits: Trial keys: 1,000 API calls/month on Chat. Chat family (Command A+, A, A Reasoning, A Translate, A Vision, R+, R, R7B, North Mini Code): 20 requests/min. Embed: 2,000 inputs/min (image embed 5 inputs/min). Rerank: 10 requests/min. EmbedJob: 5 requests/min. Tokenize: 100 requests/min. Parse: 500 requests/min. Audio Transcriptions: 5 requests/min. Default for anything else: 500 requests/min. Note: production keys are also capped at 1,000 calls/month on newer model variants such as Command A Reasoning.
path: dashboard.cohere.com/welcome/register → sign up → API Keys → copy the trial key. Cohere's docs state trial usage is free for anyone who simply creates an account.
code:
import cohere

co = cohere.ClientV2("xxx")

r = co.chat(
    model="command-a",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}],
)
print(r.message.content[0].text)
verdict: The most lopsided free tier here. As a chat API, 1,000 calls a month is a rounding error — you will burn it in an afternoon. As an embeddings and rerank provider, though, the per-month cap does not apply and you get 2,000 embed inputs/min and 10 rerank requests/min for free, which is plenty to wire up real RAG. Take the key for Rerank specifically, and plan to pay the moment you need generate.
best_for: Evaluating Cohere before a paid plan

name: NVIDIA NIM (build.nvidia.com)
tagline: Free endpoints on frontier open models — but NVIDIA publishes no numbers, so treat this as a sandbox, not a quota you can plan around.
quota: unknown — NVIDIA advertises "Free serverless APIs for development" and tags individual models with a "Free Endpoint" label, but does not publish a credit amount, token budget or monthly allowance anywhere in its public docs.
limits: unknown — no published RPM, TPM or daily cap. Models confirmed carrying a Free Endpoint label as of 2026-08-29 include moonshotai/kimi-k3, deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-pro-0813, nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b and nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b. Some free endpoints carry active deprecation notices, so availability is per-model and can disappear on short notice.
path: build.nvidia.com → sign in → open a model page → Get API Key → call the integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1 endpoint with an nvapi- key.
code:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key="nvapi-xxx",
    base_url="https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1",
)

r = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}],
)
print(r.choices[0].message.content)
verdict: Genuinely free access to large open models through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, which is rare — but it is the least documented offer on this page. No published credits, no published rate limits, no stated position on commercial use, and individual endpoints get deprecated with two weeks' notice. Fine for exploration; do not build anything you cannot migrate in an afternoon.
best_for: Trying large open models without a GPU
Evaluating NVIDIA-optimised builds of open weights
